newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 22.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The 50,000 investors burnt by the collapse in 1990 of Australia's former largest mortgage trust, Estate Mortgage, are to receive compensation from Burns Philp & Company Ltd who have agreed to pay a A$120 million settlement. The deal follows a A$31 million settlement in April with the trust's former auditors, Priestley & Morris, with the A$150 million recovered so far, forming the largest commercial settlement in Australia's history. Page 1.

The six-week strike at Rio Tinto's Hunter Valley mine is set to end at midnight tonight following a breakthrough in negotiations which saw the Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) offering to end industrial action if mine management ceaed using managerial employees and office workers to drive trucks and mine coal. Export coal will be transported out of the mine this morning with CFMEU members agreeing to handle it before they formally return to work. Page 1.

The Federal Government is to pay about $A20 million to a reprocessing plant in the US to take 690 of the 1,6000 spent nuclear fuel rods stored at the Lucal Heights reactor in Sydney. The decision was made by Cabinet last week and will relieve pressure onstorage space at Lucas Heights which is at maximum capacity. Page 3.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello, speaking on the ABC's 7:30 Report last night, has attacked a proposal by Prime Minister John Howard to form free trade zones across Australia. The plan proposed by Mr Howard on his visit to Newcastle last week offers tax incentives to companies if they invest in a marked zone. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Workers at Rio Tinto's Hunter Valley No. 1 mine will vote today on union leader's recommendation they return to work for 21 days pending further negotiations on an enterprise agreement. The six-week strike has delayed the export of over A$35 million worh of coal to Asian markets. Page 1.

A Value's Bank Research Centre and George Patterson Bates survey of 1100 consumers has identified a set of eight consumer personality profiles based on behaviour, values and demographics. The largest of these is the adventurous group made up of men in thir late 30s, single with above average incomes who comprise 27 per cent of "discretionary" shoppers, people who spend money on things other than the basic necessities. Page 1.

In its preliminary response to the Industry Commission's April report recommending a number of reforms to health care, the Federal Government is believed to have proposed a cost saving measure allowing private health consumers to drop rehabilitation and plliative care from health insurance packages. The suggestion has raised fears that Australia's non-discriminatory insurance system will be dismantled. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has admitted the leaking of a confidential Australian report on the South Pacific was "deeply insulting" but has refused to issue a formal apology to regional politicians subjected to scathing personal criticism. As part f the fall-out to Australia's image in the South Pacific, sources have said a similar New Zealand report describes Costello as "pugnacious" and "aggressive". Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Police have rescued a new-born baby girl abandoned on a beach near Batesman Bay in southern NSW. The baby named "Pretty" survived an overnight temperature of zero. Police were led to the baby by the mother's eight year old niece who had witnessed the birh. Page 1

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has admitted a major security breach by his department was responsible for the leaking of a confidential report which contained criticisms of regional leaders. Costello said yesterday that an investigation would be carried out by Treasury officials and appropriate action would be brought against those responsible for the security breach. Page 1.

Following seven-years of legal tangles Burns Philp and Co yesterday agreed to pay $A116 million in compensation to over 45,000 investors in the Estate Mortgage trust which collapsed in 1990. The settlement by Burns Philp who acted as trustee for the Estte Morgan trusts is equal to about 20 cents in the dollar to investors original input. Page 1.

In imitation of a successful Melbourne project NSW Premier Bob Carr will launch a body called the "Committee for Sydney" on August 19. Established in response to business concerns about Sydney's economic performance, the Committee will have a mandate to promote projects ranging from urban planning, tourism, the arts and law and order. Page 1.
THE AGE

The Australian Society of Certified Practising Accountants and the Institute of Chartered Accountants in Australia have urged Vic Premier Jeff Kennett to backdown from the most controversial proposals to change the role of the State's auditor-general. Intead they have proposed a compromise that will maintain the auditor-general's control over auditing the public service while allowing private firms to tender for the work as his agents. Page 1.

Phyllis Chan, the mother of murdered schoolgirl Karmein Chan yesterday told the County Court how she feared for her life when an attacker assaulted her outside her home. Chan said she pleaded with the disguised assailant saying she was Karmein Chan's mother but he brutally hit her many times with a stick. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello conceded yesterday that a leaked Government report could be interpreted as deeply insulting to South Pacific nations but refused to offer a formal apology. Costello said that investigations had uncovered lapses in security at a Cairns conference last week and that appropriate action would be taken against the Treasury Department officials responsible. Page 1.

The Vic Government has bungled negotiations with Asian shipping companies which would have seen the building of a third container terminal at Port Phillip Bay. If successful the project would have greatly expanded Melbourne's role as a domestic transport centre and have promoted trade links with Asia. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
